thread:
maya: Heads-up — canary in eu-west showing ~35ms higher p95 for text-gen path after yesterday's runtime rollout.
maya: Repro: curl -X POST "https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{\"prompt\":\"test\"}' (DMing creds).
owen: saw this on warmup dashboards. KV cache hit-rate in eu cluster dropped from ~92% -> ~78% around the rollout.
sasha: kernel selection flipped to 'fast-matmul-v2' on eu nodes (optimizer picked it for long seqs). Could the kernel change affect batch formation heuristics?
nikhil: profiling confirms a correlation: after kernel swap, avg micro-batch emitted by continuous-batcher went 1.9 -> 3.7 for the same arrival pattern. The batcher is waiting longer to form kernel-friendly sizes.
maya: that matches the timeline. increased batch sizes caused longer queue wait; once eu concurrency hit, soft-affinity spill kicked in and requests spilled cross-zone, hurting local KV hit-rates.
owen: logs show spill events to us-west at 03:14:22 with soft-affinity score drop. snippet:
```
[03:14:22] spill=1 target=us-west reason=queue-depth>threshold soft_affinity_score=0.42
```
sasha: and cross-zone requests miss local KV cache, so warmup is slower -> p95 regress.
maya: proposed mitigation plan (short):
- rollback kernel selection on eu nodes to 'fast-matmul-v1' until heuristics tuned
- tune continuous-batcher for eu: lower max_wait_ms 12 -> 7, set token_budget_per_zone = 0.65
- add per-kernel hint: fast-matmul-v2 prefer batch_threshold=4 to avoid micro-batch growth
- temporarily increase eu reserved headroom by +10% to reduce spill risk
owen: +1 to rollback and per-kernel hint. also recommend we gate the changes to canary first (eu-canary only). watch cost impact: lower wait reduces batching efficiency vs latency.
sasha: canary-only A/B for the batcher tweak sounds good. deploy-bot: starting canary rollout with config name eur-batcher-2026-03-18.
deploy-bot: rollout status: zones updated 1/3, monitoring: eu.p95, eu.kv.hit_rate, crosszone.spill_count.
nikhil: I'll run an offline profiling job emulating our seq_len distribution and token-rate to reproduce batch growth; I'll post flamegraphs and kernel timings in ~30m.
maya: I'll open a small PR to revert kernel selection and apply the batcher knobs for canary. Adding notes in PR about regression metrics to watch.
owen: after we push, keep an eye on cost vs latency tradeoff. if p95 recovers but costs spike, we may prefer per-model overrides instead of global rollbacks.
sasha: tagging @eng-sre for alerting on regressions and spill count.
eng-sre-bot: created alert eu.p95.regress (threshold +30ms) and eu.kv.hit_rate_drop (>5% drop).
maya: thanks — will follow up with results once canary finishes.
